5. Create Your First Trail
Trails are our reinvention of a pull request. From a single project view, you can now track discussions, investigate related sessions, and make changes across multiple repositories at once. From your repository root, create your trail:

entire trail create --title "My first Entire trail"

This creates a new trail and links the current branch. Check that the trail is created:

entire trail show 

Any new changes, sessions, and checkpoints in this branch will automatically be linked to your Trail. Start your agent and give it a small task:

Create a file named first-trail.md with a short note explaining that this is my first Entire Trail.

When the agent finishes, commit and push the change:

git add first-trail.md
git commit -m "Add first checkpoint in new Trail"
git push origin my-first-entire-trail

When prompted to link this commit to session context, select Y. You have now linked your first checkpoint to your new Trail! To learn more about trails, see Trails overview.
</pasted_content id="5694">

A trail captures project intent across repositories and branches. Manage intent and discussions on the whole trail; use --repo and --branch to select context for checkout, sessions, findings, and approvals.

Usage:
  entire trail [flags]
  entire trail [command]

Available Commands:
  approvals       List approval decisions on a trail
  approve         Approve a trail
  attachment      Upload, list, and remove images for a trail's description
  checkout        Check out a trail's branch
  ci-pr           Create or link the GitHub pull request that runs CI
  comment         Discuss the whole trail across repositories
  create          Create a trail and publish its branch
  finding         Manage a trail's agent findings
  link            Link a repository branch to a trail
  list            List trails in a project
  merge           Merge one of a trail's changes into its base
  ready           Mark a trail ready for review
  rerun-review    Review a trail's current head again
  resume          Resume a trail's agent session
  retarget        Change the base branch a trail merges into
  sessions        List the agent sessions behind a trail's commits
  show            Show trail intent and its repositories and branches
  stack           Show the pull request stack a trail belongs to
  timeline        Show a trail's activity: commits, reviews, findings, and approvals
  unlink          Unlink a repository branch without deleting its work
  update          Update project intent and lifecycle
  update-branch   Merge the base branch into a trail's branch
  watch           Tail events for a trail's selected repository branch
trail list requires --project gh/<owner> or et/<project>; --repo is only a filter within that project

content.text:
Step 5 is done. Your first checkpoint is now linked to your trail.

- **Trail:** you'd already created "My first Entire trail" (#1), so I didn't make a second one. It's linked to your `jerry` branch: https://entire.com/gh/nougify/-/trails/1
- **Commit:** I added `first-trail.md` and committed it as `5d88d68`. Entire attached checkpoint `01M6W8SM97AMHNRHJ4EDDGXCGC` on its own, so the Y/N prompt from the guide never came up.
- **Push:** I pushed to `origin jerry` instead of `my-first-entire-trail`, because `jerry` is the branch your trail is linked to. The trail's activity history shows the commit.

One thing to know: `entire trail show` with no arguments returned a 403 "no read access" error. `entire trail show 1 --project gh/nougify` works fine. If you want the short form to work, try `entire login`.
